PC: Perform a rapid assessment: CAB, vital signs
Perform a focused history and examination
Place the patient on cardiac monitor
Cautious correction of hypokalemia, hypophosphatemia and hyperglycemia
Gastrointestinal decontamination with activated charcoal once vomiting controlled
Request appropriate tests: Lab, EKG, Chest x-ray, ABG
MK: Develop and discuss differential diagnosis for patient presentation including cocaine/amphetamine use, beta-2 agonist overdose, salicylate overdose, and sepsis
Identification of the causative agent: Theophylline poisoning
SBP: Consultation with Toxicology for treatment plan review
Referral to Nephrology for consideration of hemodialysis
